query_details.query: What is the territorial extent and commencement of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
query_details.answer:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint, with different dates possible for different States and different provisions of this Act. Any reference in any provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

Relevant Act and Section Citations:
- The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
- Section 1 - Short Title, Extent, Commencement And Application

query_details.query: How is a defect in goods defined under consumer protection law?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 2(10) of The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, "defect" means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law.

Relevant Act and Section Citations:
- **Act:** The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
- **Section:** Section 2(10)

query_details.query: What constitutes a deficiency of service for a service provider?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 2(11) of The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a "deficiency" means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise. This includes acts of negligence or omission or commission by such person that cause loss or injury to the consumer, as well as deliberate withholding of relevant information.

Act: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Section: Section 2(11)

query_details.query: Does the Code on Wages prohibit paying different wages to male and female employees for equal work?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 3 of The Code on Wages, 2019, there shall be no discrimination in an establishment or any unit thereof among employees on the ground of gender in matters relating to the same work or work of similar nature. Specifically, subsection (2) states that no employer shall make any discrimination on the ground of sex while recruiting any employee for the same work or work of similar nature.

Thus, based on the provided legal context, paying different wages to male and female employees for equal work is prohibited under The Code on Wages, 2019, Section 3.

Relevant Act and Section citations:
- **Act:** The Code on Wages, 2019
- **Section:** Section 3

query_details.query: What factors must the government consider when fixing minimum wage rates for workers?
query_details.answer:
The appropriate Government must consider several factors when fixing minimum wage rates for workers under Section 6(3)(c) of The Code on Wages, 2019. Specifically, these factors include:

- The arduousness of work such as temperature or humidity normally difficult to bear.
- Hazardous occupations or processes.
- Underground work.

These considerations are aimed at ensuring that employees receive a minimum rate of wages that accounts for the nature and conditions under which they perform their jobs.

- **Act:** The Code on Wages, 2019

query_details.query: What is the role and powers of conciliation officers in industrial disputes?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 43 of The Industrial Relations Code, 2020, conciliation officers are appointed by the appropriate Government with the duty to mediate in and promote the settlement of industrial disputes. They can be appointed for a specified area or industry, either permanently or for a limited period.

Regarding their powers, under Section 49 of The Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a conciliation officer has the power to enforce the attendance of any person and examine them or compel the production of documents. This authority is similar to that vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

For more detailed information on their roles and powers, please refer to Sections 43 and 49 of The Industrial Relations Code, 2020.

query_details.query: How is the Central Board of Trustees for Provident Fund constituted under the Social Security Code?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 4(1) of The Code on Social Security, 2020, the Central Government may, by notification, constitute a Board of Trustees for the Employees' Provident Fund. This board is called the Central Board and will consist of:
- A Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson appointed by the Central Government
- Not more than five persons appointed by organizations recognized by the Central Government in this behalf
- The Central Provident Fund Commissioner, ex officio

Relevant Act and Section Citations: 
The Code on Social Security, 2020, Section 4

query_details.query: How is a valid sale of immovable property defined under the Transfer of Property Act?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 54 of The Transfer of Property Act, 1882, "Sale" defined includes the sale of immovable property. A valid sale of immovable property is made through a contract between two parties mutually transferring ownership from one party to another for valuable consideration.

query_details.query: What are the legal requirements for creating a lease of immovable property?
query_details.answer:
According to Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent, can be made only by a registered instrument. All other leases of immovable property may be made either by a registered instrument or by an oral agreement accompanied by the delivery of possession.

- The Transfer of Property Act, 1882

query_details.query: Can a landlord evict a tenant if the tenant pays rent regularly?
query_details.answer:
Based on the provided legal context, Section 38 of The Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 states that no ordinary eviction (ejectment) is to be made if a fair rent has been paid. This suggests that a landlord may not evict a tenant who pays regular rent at the fair rate.
